solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cream bun consumed in lunch outing

indicators.note: something consumed in a phrase is swallowed inside it, so the answer sits within the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys a cream bun on a lunchtime trip out.
explanation.walkthrough: CHOU sits across lun(CH OU)ting; it is the French word for a choux pastry bun.
explanation.definitionFit: A chou is a small round choux-pastry puff, typically filled with cream, so it is a cream bun.

clue.text: Fundamentally strengthen e.g. dam, dry, protected by spar

indicators.note: something protected by another is shielded within it, so it goes inside

blocks.note: a dam was a small Indian copper coin
a boom is a spar on a ship
TT is teetotal, dry

explanation.surface: Reinforce a dam from below, keeping it dry with a spar.
explanation.walkthrough: Dam looks like the river barrier, which suits the surface, but it is an old Indian coin made of copper.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper-bottom means to sheathe a ship's hull in copper, so to make something sound from the bottom up.

clue.text: Commotion with left replacing right in haste

indicators.note: replacing means taking the place of, so one letter goes in where another comes out

blocks.note: a hurry is haste
L is the abbreviation for left
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A rush of political commotion as the left takes over from the right.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one R of HURRY becomes L.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurly, as in hurly-burly, means an uproar or tumult.

clue.text: Budget? Chancellor's last cut initially in the bag

indicators.note: cut at the start means a letter is removed from the beginning of the word
'last' keeps only the last letter of 'Chancellor'

blocks.note: a budget was a name for the rudder of a barge
last letter of chancellor; this is the letter taken away

explanation.surface: The Budget finally has the Chancellor's last measures slashed, and it is all wrapped up.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags an unusual sense of Budget: a barge's rudder. 'In the bag' looks like an idiom, but bag is the dairy farmer's word.
explanation.definitionFit: A cow's udder is known as her bag, the milk-holding organ.

clue.text: Cavities

blocks.note: the only words printed: this is the competition clue, for which solvers write their own

explanation.walkthrough: In an Azed competition puzzle one entry is given only as a bare definition, and entrants compete to write the best clue for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers are enclosed spaces in the body or an organ, such as the chambers of the heart, so hollow cavities.

clue.text: Boss issuing repeated call to attend – no charge included

indicators.note: included means placed inside, so these letters go within the other part

blocks.note: ho is a call for attention, and it is repeated
NC is the abbreviation for no charge

explanation.surface: A manager keeps calling staff in, insisting there's no fee.
explanation.definitionFit: A honcho, from Japanese, is a leader or person in charge, the same as a boss.

clue.text: Sitar player getting into first half of raga soaring rapturously? (6, two words)

indicators.note: the first half of a four-letter word is its opening two letters
soaring goes upward, and in a down clue that reads the letters bottom to top
getting into means entering, so one part sits inside the other

blocks.note: the first two letters of raga
Ravi Shankar was the famous Indian sitar player

explanation.surface: A sitarist soars ecstatically into the first part of a raga.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a French phrase: à ravir means delightfully or ravishingly.
explanation.definitionFit: A ravir is French for enchantingly, wonderfully well, the ravishing manner of rapture.

clue.text: Youngster mounted on pre-eminent stallion maybe presenting rodeo challenge?

indicators.note: mounted means climbed up, and in a down clue going upward reads the word backwards

blocks.note: a cub is a young animal
the king is the pre-eminent figure

explanation.surface: A young rider astride a champion stallion is in for a tough rodeo ride.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the animal: a stallion that presents a rodeo challenge is one that bucks.
explanation.definitionFit: A bucking horse leaps and kicks to throw its rider, the challenge of the rodeo bronco ride.

clue.text: Interval arranged around middle of opera, going on for ever

indicators.note: the middle of a five-letter word is its third letter
arranged means put in a new order, so the letters are reordered
around means surrounding, so the reordered letters wrap the other part

blocks.note: the centre letter of opera
interval reordered

explanation.surface: An interval during an opera that seems to drag on for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: The E goes on the outside of the reworked INTERVAL, at its front.
explanation.definitionFit: Eviternal is a rare word meaning eternal or everlasting, so continuing for ever.

clue.text: Take fresh sample from a tree, gnarled, edging street

indicators.note: gnarled means twisted and knotted, so the words before it are rearranged
edging means forming the border round something, so it surrounds the next part

blocks.note: a tree rearranged
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Take another sample from a knotty old tree at the roadside.
explanation.walkthrough: A sample here is a taste of food, not a sample of wood.
explanation.definitionFit: To retaste is to taste again, taking a fresh sample of food or drink.

clue.text: Excessive fattiness ruined the orator in the main

indicators.note: in places the speaker's words inside the last part before the shake-up
something ruined is wrecked out of shape, so all these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the main is the open sea
taken as written

explanation.surface: An overweight speaker came to grief in the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The orator goes into the sea first and then the whole lot is rearranged, since the letters of SEA are spread through the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Steatorrhoea is the medical term for excess fat in the faeces, a condition of fattiness.

clue.text: Make love amid dissolute routs, alfresco

indicators.note: dissolute means loose and disordered, so the word after it is to be broken up and rearranged
amid places the first part in the middle of the second, surrounded on both sides

blocks.note: the letters of routs, rearranged
DO is make, and love is O, the zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: An invitation to make love among the debauched crowds in the open air.
explanation.walkthrough: DO plus O go into the reworked ROUTS: OUT(DOO)RS. A rout is an old word for a riotous crowd or party.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfresco means in the open air, which is exactly what outdoors means as an adverb.

clue.text: Village abroad? One making return journey as reminder

indicators.note: a word that makes a return journey travels back the way it came, so it is read from end to start

blocks.note: a dorp is a South African village or small town

explanation.surface: A traveller in a foreign village heads home, prompted by something.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks 'abroad' as pointing to a foreign word: DORP is Afrikaans, from Dutch.
explanation.definitionFit: A prod is a nudge or poke to jog someone's memory, so a reminder in the figurative sense.

clue.text: Being obsessive, name distinctive rock type

blocks.note: anal, short for anally retentive, means fussily obsessive
to cite is to name or mention

explanation.surface: A geologist is fussy about naming a particular kind of rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Analcite (analcime) is a white zeolite mineral found in igneous rocks, a characteristic mineral type.

clue.text: Former trader, line fixed in jetty

indicators.note: something fixed in a structure is set inside it, so one part goes within the other

blocks.note: a pier is a jetty
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A merchant of old with a fishing line set up on the jetty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Former' tells the solver this sense is obsolete: a plier was once one who plies a trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Plying a trade means working at it, so in the old sense a plier was a tradesman or dealer.

clue.text: Colouring matter favoured with density I sent for

blocks.note: in means popular, favoured
D is the symbol for density
if I sent for someone, I got them in

explanation.surface: Someone sends for a favoured, dense dye.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigotin is the blue chemical compound that gives indigo dye its colour.

clue.text: Measure of cloud cover, fair, that evens out

indicators.note: putting the even-placed letters out leaves only the odd-placed ones of the word

blocks.note: OK means fair or middling
the first and third letters of that

explanation.surface: A weather forecaster's measure of cloud that averages things out to fair.
explanation.definitionFit: An okta is the meteorologists' unit of cloud cover, one eighth of the sky covered.

clue.text: Like brightest stars, making name that is special in dancing hits

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so the word they describe is rearranged
in places the preceding letters inside the rearranged word

blocks.note: hits rearranged
N is the abbreviation for name
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
S is the abbreviation for special

explanation.surface: Top stars make a name for themselves with special dance hits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars' tempts towards celebrities, but the definition is literal: stars in the sky that shine most brightly.
explanation.definitionFit: The brightest stars gleam the most, so shiniest is the superlative that describes them.

clue.text: Revolutionary, executed maybe protecting his leader, brittle when heated

indicators.note: protecting means wrapping round, so one part is placed around another

blocks.note: a Red is a communist revolutionary
being shot is one form of execution
his refers back to the revolutionary, whose first letter is wanted

explanation.surface: A revolutionary is executed, perhaps while shielding his commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His leader' means the leader of 'Revolutionary', its first letter R, not the H of his; it goes inside SHOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Red-short describes metal, especially iron with too much sulphur, that becomes brittle at red heat.

clue.text: Hammer maybe decapitated copy in gutted engine

indicators.note: decapitated means the head is removed, so the first letter goes
gutted means emptied of its insides, leaving just the outer letters
in places the shortened word inside the outer pair

blocks.note: the outer letters of engine
a carbon is a copy

explanation.surface: A sledgehammer, perhaps, is a replica part fitted inside a stripped-down engine.
explanation.walkthrough: Hammer is not the tool but the malleus, a bone of the middle ear.
explanation.definitionFit: The hammer or malleus is one of the small bones of the inner ear, so an example of an earbone.

clue.text: Snuffs to sprinkle without getting up

indicators.note: getting up means rising, and in a down clue that reads the letters from the bottom

blocks.note: set in the sense of sprinkle, to stud or dot over
sans is without

explanation.surface: Someone takes snuff and sprinkles it without standing up.
explanation.walkthrough: Snuffs is a noun here: a snaste is the burnt end of a candle wick.
explanation.definitionFit: Snaste is a dialect word for a candle's snuff, the charred part of the wick.

clue.text: One who'll fix faulty gas rings wasting good energy

indicators.note: faulty things are not in working order, so these letters are rearranged
wasting one thing in favour of another means one letter is spent and the other takes its place

blocks.note: taken as written
G is the abbreviation for good
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A repairman who'll mend broken gas rings while squandering good energy.
explanation.walkthrough: One G of GAS RINGS is dropped and E added, and the result is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To assign is to fix or appoint something, such as a date or a task, so an assigner is one who fixes it.

clue.text: One stocking, second put on matador a bit short?

indicators.note: a bit short means lacking a little at the end, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a torero is a bullfighter

explanation.surface: Someone wearing hosiery, perhaps a bullfighter in his outfit that is slightly too small.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on' looks like dressing up, matching 'stocking', but it just means placed before.
explanation.definitionFit: A storer is one who stores or stocks up goods, keeping a supply.

clue.text: Climbing pear, eastern, displaying flower

indicators.note: climbing goes upward, and in a down clue the letters then read bottom to top

blocks.note: a nelis is a winter pear
E is the abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: An eastern pear tree climbing a wall is in bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Silene is the catchfly or campion genus, plants with pink or white flowers.

clue.text: Translation of Crito includes empty talk describing a climax

indicators.note: a translation turns a text into new form, so these letters are reworked
includes means takes inside, so the next part sits within the reworked word

blocks.note: Crito, a dialogue of Plato, rearranged
gas is idle, empty talk

explanation.surface: A version of Plato's Crito pads out its account of the dramatic high point with waffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Orgastic means relating to orgasm, so the word is used of a sexual climax.

clue.text: Knight e.g. displaying distinctive character, following Lancelot's lead

indicators.note: a word's lead is its opening letter, so only the first one is kept
following means coming after, so the character piece is written second, behind the knight's initial

blocks.note: the opening letter of Lancelot
an aura is a distinctive atmosphere or quality

explanation.surface: A knight of the Round Table shows his character, following Sir Lancelot's example.
explanation.walkthrough: Knight is not a chivalric knight but Dame Laura Knight, the English painter. AURA follows L.
explanation.definitionFit: Laura Knight was a celebrated twentieth-century English painter, so a Knight by surname is a Laura.

clue.text: Inundation well above odd ones appearing in Tees

indicators.note: odd ones are the letters in odd-numbered places, first and third

blocks.note: a spa is a mineral spring or well
the first and third letters of Tees

explanation.surface: Floodwater rising high on the River Tees.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'above' puts the first part on top. The Tees is a river in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A spate is a sudden flood in a river, a rush of water, so an inundation.

clue.text: What's uprooting wort from historic field? Rats!

indicators.note: uprooting a plant pulls it out entirely, so the word naming the plant is removed

blocks.note: Bosworth Field, the 1485 battle where Richard III died
wort is a plant, and these letters are taken out

explanation.surface: Someone asks what is pulling up the plants in an old battlefield, and blames vermin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rats!' looks like the answer to the question, but it is the definition, an exclamation of disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: Bosh is an exclamation dismissing something as nonsense, the same scornful sense as rats used as an interjection.

clue.text: One playing around with characters, a feature of moral philosophy

indicators.note: a feature of something is part of it, so the answer is found inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters bridge the two words

explanation.surface: An ethicist toys with ideas about character, central to moral philosophy.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters are found in mo(RAL PH)ilosophy. Ralph is the leading boy in Golding's Lord of the Flies, a novel whose themes are moral.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph is one of the boys playing on the island with the other characters of Lord of the Flies.

clue.text: On the wagon, imbibing nothing, soak turned journo was staggering

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the following part goes inside
turned round, the word reads from its end to its start

blocks.note: TT, teetotal, is on the wagon
O is nought
to ret flax is to soak it
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A drunk who went teetotal and took up journalism was still unsteady on his feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soak' reads as a drunkard, fitting the surface, but here it is the verb ret, to steep flax.
explanation.definitionFit: To totter is to walk unsteadily, so tottered matches was staggering in tense and sense.

clue.text: Feature of shores, lacustrine or palustrine? This splinter possibly

indicators.note: possibly means in one arrangement of several, so the letters are mixed up
this points to the answer itself, which with the next word makes up the letters, so those must be removed again

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; these letters are taken away

explanation.surface: A question about a feature of lake shores or marsh shores, with a hint about a splinter.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite: the answer plus SPLINTER can be rearranged into OR PALUSTRINE. Lacustrine means of lakes, palustrine of marshes.
explanation.definitionFit: Urao is natural sodium carbonate (trona) found as a crust on the shores of lakes, as in Venezuela.

clue.text: Worship opening with head of episcopate, about monarch, absent

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the earlier letters are put round what follows
'head of' keeps only the first letter of 'episcopate'

blocks.note: a vent is an opening
first letter of episcopate
ER, Elizabeth Regina
a. is an abbreviation for absent

explanation.surface: Worship begins with the bishop, while the king is away.
explanation.walkthrough: Chambers gives a. as an abbreviation of absent; ER is Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: To venerate is to regard with deep reverence, a synonym of worship as a verb.

clue.text: Safeguard introduced by merchant navy for fencing contests

indicators.note: something introduced by another is brought in between it, so it goes inside

blocks.note: MN is the abbreviation for Merchant Navy
to ensure is to safeguard or make safe

explanation.surface: Merchant seamen bring in protection to put round contested territory.
explanation.definitionFit: Mensuren are the formal sword duels of German student fraternities, so fencing bouts.

clue.text: A cause son's abandoned in part of city?

indicators.note: abandoned means left behind, so these letters are dropped from the word

blocks.note: taken as written
a reason is a cause
taken as written; removed

explanation.surface: A troubled cause led a son to be left in some district.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that a district of a city is just one example of an area.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is a region or district, such as a part of a city.
